text: We evaluated a two-phase curriculum that trains on confident weak-labeled examples before expanding to the full weak-labeled set, with the phase-two learning rate scaled by 0.1, using qwen2.5-0.5b as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-7b as the strong student. Across 3 seeds, the weak supervisor reached 0.67 accuracy and the strong ceiling was 0.94, while the curriculum-trained student reached a transfer accuracy of 0.67 (SE 0.04) and a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.01 (SE 0.13). The baseline PGR is 0.46, so the curriculum does not recover more of the weak-to-strong gap than the baseline; the measured PGR sits well below it, and the large standard error relative to the estimate means the value is poorly constrained. With only 3 seeds, these numbers should be treated as preliminary and no directional conclusion about the curriculum's benefit is supported. Transfer accuracy matching weak accuracy is consistent with the near-zero PGR.
